blocks.content: Explore a histogram to see how its bars group values into numeric ranges, not named categories.

blocks.title: Read a bucket and its count

blocks.content: Open **Histogram Examples** and keep the full dashboard visible.
Find **Random Timeseries Data**, then **Time series + Auto buckets**. Scroll through the dashboard if needed. The histogram reuses the time-series panel's numeric samples.
In **Time series + Auto buckets**, read the numeric ranges on the horizontal axis and the counts on the vertical axis. Hover over a bar to inspect its bucket and count.

Compare a taller bar with a shorter one. The taller bar contains more observations in its numeric range; it doesn't necessarily contain the largest values. Position along the horizontal axis identifies the value range.

A histogram answers "How are these numeric values distributed?" Unlike the library bar chart, its bars group numbers into ranges rather than named categories. It summarizes the selected observations without showing when each one occurred.
You've read bucket ranges and counts. Next, add time to inspect how a distribution changes.
